name: Construction and permanent financing norms (US, Oct 2026)
method: Rates are anchored to FRED market data as of 2026-10-21/24 (SOFR, prime, Fed target, Treasuries). Lender spreads, LTC, fees and draw-balance factors are derived conventions, not survey data: the web-search budget ran out before a public spread/LTC survey (e.g. CBRE, MBA, Trepp) could be located. Verify with current term sheets. All values are decimals.

items.name: Construction loan all-in interest rate (floating, 2026)

range.method: All-in = 1-month SOFR (about 3.89%: e1, e2) + lender spread. No public, current survey of construction-loan spreads was found, so the spreads are an assumption: bank/regional-bank construction ~SOFR+2.50 to +3.50 (often quoted as prime, e3, = SOFR+3.1); debt-fund/non-bank ~SOFR+4.0 to +5.0. Low = 3.89+2.50 = 6.4%. Mid = prime, 7.00% (3.89+3.11). High = 3.89+4.60 = about 8.5% (non-bank, higher leverage). Tight CLD standards (e6) argue against the low end for spec projects. Verify spreads with a lender quote.

items.notes: Floating rate. Rate caps or floors and SOFR moves over an 18-30 month draw period can shift the realized rate by +/-50-100 bp.

items.name: Construction loan-to-cost (LTC)

range.method: Regulatory loan-to-value ceilings (e5): 80% for commercial/multifamily construction, 85% for 1-4 family. Lenders size well inside these and usually also cap LTC. With CLD standards at the tighter end of their range (e6), bank senior construction loans are assumed at 50-65% LTC and up to 70-75% with recourse, strong sponsors or non-bank lenders. Mid 60%. Agency/HUD 221(d)(4) programs go higher, but no source page could be retrieved this session (not cited).

items.notes: Equity first: the loan funds only after the (1 - LTC) equity is spent, as the engine models.

items.name: Construction loan origination fee (% of loan commitment)

range.method: Industry convention of 0.5-1.5 points (1 point = 1% of commitment), paid at closing; mid 1.0 point. No public survey was retrievable this session. Excludes lender legal, inspection and title (budget those as soft costs) and any exit fee (0-1%) charged by non-bank lenders.

items.notes: Applied to the loan commitment at close.

items.name: Average outstanding balance as share of loan commitment (construction + lease-up carry)

range.method: Monthly simulation (scratch model): 20% of cost up front (land/soft), remaining hard cost on an S-curve (smoothstep), equity first, then loan draws, then the loan held fully drawn through lease-up until takeout. Average balance / commitment over construction + lease-up: 18-mo build + 6-mo lease-up = 0.54-0.59 (LTC 55-70%); 18 + 12 = 0.63-0.67; 24 + 6 = 0.50-0.56; 24 + 12 = 0.59-0.63; 12 + 12 = 0.69-0.72. Range 0.50-0.70, mid 0.60. Matches the common 55-65% rule of thumb when interest is figured over construction + lease-up.

items.notes: Shortcut check only: interest = loan x rate x (construction + lease-up months)/12 x this factor. The engine itself simulates monthly draws.

items.name: Average outstanding balance, construction period only (equity first)

range.method: Same simulation, averaged over the construction months only (no lease-up). LTC 55% = 0.38, 60% = 0.40, 65% = 0.43, 70% = 0.45, nearly independent of a 12-24 month duration. Pari-passu funding (equity and loan drawn pro rata) would give about 0.60 instead.

items.notes: Use when the shortcut covers construction months only.

items.name: Interest reserve convention
items.value: Construction interest is capitalized: an interest-reserve line inside the loan budget pays monthly interest on the drawn balance until completion or stabilization, so interest is part of total project cost. It is sized as rate x average outstanding balance x (construction + lease-up months)/12, plus a cushion for rate moves (a floating loan with no cap). Equity funds first; the loan fee is paid at close and usually financed.
items.method: Standard lender structure for floating-rate construction loans. The engine models this directly (monthly draws, equity first, capitalized interest).

items.name: Permanent / takeout loan rate (fixed, 7-10 year)

range.method: 10-year Treasury about 5.0-5.3% (e7; October 2026 average 5.19%) + spread. Spreads are an assumption (no public current survey retrieved): agency multifamily / life-company ~+1.4 to +1.8; bank / CMBS ~+1.9 to +2.5. Low = 5.10+1.40 = 6.5%. Mid = 5.19+1.90 = about 7.1%. High = 5.19+2.50 = about 7.7%.

items.notes: Used for stabilized-value or refinance checks, not by the construction budget. exitCapRate guidance is out of scope here (no sourced 2026 cap-rate survey retrieved).

source.title: Secured Overnight Financing Rate (SOFR)
source.publisher: Federal Reserve Bank of St. Louis (FRED)

evidence.scopeNotes: Overnight SOFR (data: Federal Reserve Bank of New York). Rose from 3.50 (2026 low) to about 3.9 during 2026. Floating construction loans reset monthly, so the all-in rate moves with SOFR.

source.title: 30-Day Average SOFR (SOFR30DAYAVG)
source.publisher: Federal Reserve Bank of St. Louis (FRED)

evidence.scopeNotes: Proxy for the 1-month Term SOFR index used in most construction loans (Term SOFR itself is a licensed CME rate, not on FRED).

source.title: Bank Prime Loan Rate (DPRIME)
source.publisher: Federal Reserve Bank of St. Louis (FRED)

evidence.scopeNotes: Community and regional banks often price construction loans at prime or prime plus a margin; prime = SOFR + about 3.1 points today.

source.title: Federal Funds Target Range - Upper Limit (DFEDTARU)
source.publisher: Federal Reserve Bank of St. Louis (FRED)

source.title: 12 CFR Appendix A to Subpart A of Part 365 - Interagency Guidelines for Real Estate Lending Policies
source.publisher: Legal Information Institute, Cornell Law School (text of FDIC regulation)

evidence.quote: Supervisory loan-to-value limits table: Construction: Commercial, multifamily, and other nonresidential 80; 1- to 4-family residential 85; Land development 75; Raw land 65
evidence.scopeNotes: Regulatory ceiling on loan-to-VALUE for bank construction loans, not a typical loan-to-cost. Typical LTC sits well below it.

source.title: The July 2026 Senior Loan Officer Opinion Survey on Bank Lending Practices
source.publisher: Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System

evidence.quote: For CRE loans, a significant net share of banks reported that lending standards were at the tighter end of their range for CLD loans
evidence.scopeNotes: Same survey: standards for construction and land development loans 'remained basically unchanged on net', and demand for CLD loans weakened. Supports conservative LTC and spreads.

source.title: Market Yield on U.S. Treasury Securities at 10-Year Constant Maturity (DGS10)
source.publisher: Federal Reserve Bank of St. Louis (FRED)

evidence.scopeNotes: Base rate for fixed-rate permanent and agency loans.

source.title: Market Yield on U.S. Treasury Securities at 5-Year Constant Maturity (DGS5)
source.publisher: Federal Reserve Bank of St. Louis (FRED)

evidence.scopeNotes: Base rate for 5-year fixed bank and bridge-to-perm loans.
